# GEO report: quay-store **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 40–40/100, At risk Confidence: High (checked 25 of 25 points). How it's calculated: low = 12 ÷ 25 × 100 = 48. High = (12 + 0) ÷ 25 × 100 = 48. Both are capped at 40 because `robots.txt` blocks Googlebot from the whole site. Every rule could be decided from the code, so the score has no unknowns. The score is held down by three site-wide problems: - Googlebot is blocked. - Pages are rendered only in the browser. - The `` tag has no `lang`. All results are read from code, not measured on a live site. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Stop blocking Googlebot in robots.txt - **Why it matters:** Googlebot is told to stay out of every page, including the two pages your sitemap asks it to visit. This also puts a 40-point cap on the score. - **Where:** `static/robots.txt:5` - **What the code says:** `Disallow: /` (under `User-agent: Googlebot`) - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 18 ÷ 25 = **72** (GEO-009 and GEO-014 become Clear, +6 points, and the cap is lifted). ### 2. Make page content appear in the server's HTML - **Why it matters:** Many crawlers don't run JavaScript. With server rendering switched off, they receive an empty page shell. - **Where:** `src/routes/+layout.ts:1` - **What the code says:** `export const ssr = false;` - **Size:** Small (remove it, or add `export const prerender = true;`) - **Score after this:** after items 1 and 2, 21 ÷ 25 = **84**. On its own it would be 15 ÷ 25 = 60, but the cap holds the score at 40 until item 1 is done. ### 3. Add a `lang` to ``, and write the empty shop description - **Why it matters:** `lang` tells machines the page language. The empty description leaves `/shop` with no summary. - **Where:** `src/app.html:2` and `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:3` - **What the code says:** `` and `` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** after items 1 to 3, 23 ÷ 25 = **92**. On its own it would be 14 ÷ 25 = 56, held at 40 by the cap. ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and within size limits | Clear | Not run | `static/robots.txt`, plain text and valid lines | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access you intend | Problem | Not run | `static/robots.txt:5`, `Disallow: /` for Googlebot. This is site-wide, so it earns 0 | | GEO-014 | Sitemap-listed and linked pages are indexable | Problem | Not run | Both `/` and `/shop` are blocked for Googlebot by `static/robots.txt:5`. Neither has a noindex | | GEO-015 | Canonical is absolute and on your own domain | Clear | Not run | `src/routes/+page.svelte:4`, `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:4`. The domain `quay.example` matches robots.txt and the sitemap | | GEO-003 | Content is in the server HTML | Problem | Not run | `src/routes/+layout.ts:1`, `export const ssr = false;` | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD parses and has its required properties | Problem | Not run | `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:5`. The `Product` has only `name`, with no offers, review or rating | | GEO-011 | Sitemap exists and robots.txt points to it | Clear | Not run | `static/sitemap.xml`, `static/robots.txt:7` | | GEO-012 | Title, description and html lang are present | Problem | Not run | `src/app.html:2` has no `lang`, and `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:3` has an empty description. Site-wide, so it earns 0 | | GEO-016 | Key pages are reachable through normal links | Clear | Not run | `src/routes/+layout.svelte:5`, `` | | GEO-017 | Snippet limits don't conflict with AI search | Clear | Not run | `src/routes/+layout.svelte:7` uses only the scoped `data-nosnippet`. I found no page-wide `nosnippet`, and no header-setting code in the repo | | GEO-002 | Basic accessibility checks | Clear | Not run | I read the layout and the 3 pages. They have no images, the links have text, and each page has a title | | GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | Not run | No app is declared | GEO-010 (`llms.txt`) is informational only: none is present. GEO-102 is also informational only, and there is no app, so it doesn't apply. ## Other problems found - `/search` has `noindex`, which is a deliberate choice. It isn't in the sitemap or the navigation, so there's no conflict. - Your sitemap lists pages that `robots.txt` tells Googlebot not to visit (`static/sitemap.xml:3`: `https://quay.example/`). Item 1 fixes this. ## Worth considering - **Product details in the JSON-LD:** `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:5`: `"@type":"Product","name":"Bilge pump"`. A single product is described, but the page text just says "Bilge pumps, cleats and rope". If you list real products with prices, you could give each its own page and label it with price and availability. That might help machines understand what you sell. - **Product pages:** `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:9`: `

Bilge pumps, cleats and rope.

`. The shop is one short sentence. A visitor would want to see which pumps, sizes and prices, as text a machine can read. - **The "next day" delivery claim:** `src/routes/+page.svelte:7`: `

Marine parts, shipped next day

`. The page doesn't back this up with cut-off times or regions. The only delivery text is in the footer (`src/routes/+layout.svelte:7`), which is deliberately snippet-limited. - **Viewport tag:** `src/app.html:4`: ``. There's no ``, which affects how mobile pages are read. - **Main landmark and heading structure:** `src/app.html:8`: `
%sveltekit.body%
`. A `
` around the page content would help machines tell content from navigation. - **Description for `/search`:** it is noindexed on purpose, so this isn't needed. ## Can't tell from code - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs ` to check real crawlers against their published addresses. - **Live status codes:** `geopilot scan ` would confirm that `/`, `/shop` and the sitemap URLs really answer 200. That check is live only. ## Assumptions - You want search engines and AI tools to find the site. There's no `geo.config.json`, so I assumed this. - The domain is `quay.example`. It is used consistently in the canonicals, the sitemap and robots.txt, but it looks like a placeholder. Replace it with your real domain. - I treated `/` and `/shop` as the important routes. `/search` is noindexed and isn't in the sitemap or navigation. - I didn't read or run anything outside the repo's tracked files. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
